correctness.rationale: A universal length-(2R+m) superword for every target of length m forces insertion coverage to imply deletion coverage. Constructive robust witnesses prove this for m<=2 over all alphabets and m=3 over binary alphabets. When q>=3, omitting 012 from all codewords of length R+3 gives insertion coverage by the three-letter pigeonhole argument but not deletion coverage. For q=2, omitting 0110 from all codewords of length R+4 similarly works because an allegedly unavoidable 0110 would require at least R+2 occurrences of both letters and then at least 2(R+1)>R+2 ones between consecutive zeros. All cases include arbitrary R>=1; exact finite enumerations provide additional independent checks, not the proof.

value.rationale: A paper newly demonstrates that insertion and deletion covering differ, motivating the precise first length where their logical equivalence breaks. The new theorem answers that natural boundary question exactly for all radii and all alphabets and finds a sharp q=2 versus q>=3 phase transition. Three-symbol missing-subsequence avoidance explains the nonbinary onset, whereas binary words require a four-symbol obstruction. The result is not a routine code-size substitution or a finite arbitrary small instance; it is a complete structural threshold classification.
